subject: Australia — general recruitment/search services
reason: Description-backed QA explicitly shows Personnel Recruitment, Recruitment Services and bulk recruitment. v2 supplier normalization still leaves 359 normalized supplier keys across 2,130 awards, with top supplier share 6.6%. This is a genuine fragmented recruitment/search market, economically distinct from simple contractor body-shopping.
model_implication: Candidate discovery, outreach, screening, CV normalization and matching are highly automatable; public-sector recruitment/search is a major SPM asymmetric thesis. Current panel/local-entity/labour-law access remains unknown.

subject: Australia — executive search
reason: Description-backed QA explicitly identifies Executive Search Services. 118 historical awards, 40 buyers and 46 normalized supplier keys; top normalized supplier share 14.4%.
model_implication: Potentially attractive high-fee search lane, but credibility, senior-network depth and local-market knowledge may matter more than automation.

subject: Australia — digital/e-learning/platform/content
reason: QA shows genuine learning-platform/content suppliers such as Acorn PLMS, Pluralsight, B Online Learning, Cornerstone, Evolve Studios and Liberate Learning. 92 awards, 51 buyers, 56 normalized supplier keys; top normalized share 19.6%.
model_implication: Real digital-learning market and AI/content-production adjacency, but more incumbent/platform concentration than the raw v1 suggested.

subject: Australia — training design/content
reason: 162 awards and strong supplier breadth survive decomposition, but representative records include opaque/large Defence scopes and mixed training-delivery economics. More semantic segmentation is needed before treating all 162 as AI-compressible content production.
next_test: Separate instructional design/courseware/content production from instructor-led delivery and specialist military training.

subject: USA broad court-reporting v1 count
reason: Broad v1 matched office-renovation and stenographer-notebook records. Precision v2 reduces the lane from 12,478 broad matches to 5,204 strict court-reporting/deposition-service awards. Excluded records remain in canonical archive.

subject: USA — precision court reporting / deposition reporting services
reason: Precision QA contains explicit Court Reporting Services / Deposition Reporting Services with recurring agency-like winners including Planet Depos, US Legal Support, Capital Reporting, Magna Legal, eScribers and ExpertConnect. 5,204 awards, 260 buyers, 358 suppliers; median award ~$3.8k, top supplier 14.0%.
model_implication: Looks like a genuine network/agency market, operationally lean but relatively low-ticket per award; US contracting/access and certified-reporter requirements need separate analysis.

subject: USA broad interpretation v1 count
reason: Broad v1 captured radiological/technical/data interpretation. Precision linguistic rules reduce 23,666 broad matches to 1,017 language-interpretation awards. Excluded records remain available for other classifications.

subject: USA — language interpretation services
reason: Precision QA explicitly shows interpreter services, language interpretation, phone interpretation and sign-language support. 1,017 awards, 260 buyers, 216 suppliers; median ~$17.3k, top supplier share 7.6%.
model_implication: Distinct from written translation. Remote phone/video interpretation is especially compatible with a distributed interpreter-network model; human delivery limits pure AI substitution.

subject: USA — expert witness / litigation expert network intermediary
reason: Expert-witness precision lane remains 11,681 awards across 241 buyers and 2,648 suppliers, top share 4.7%. Heuristic supplier-shape analysis finds 8,017 awards / 1,754 suppliers with organization-like names versus 3,664 / 894 individual-like, and QA shows many consulting/engineering expert firms. This materially strengthens, but does not prove, an expert-network aggregation model.
next_test: Resolve winner archetypes more rigorously, identify expert-network/placement firms specifically, and compare agency margins vs direct expert contracting.
